description: Classification means forming a group based on common characteristics among given objects, numbers, or words, and separating the one that does not belong to that group (Odd One Out). This topic tests the candidate's logical ability.

sections.title: Bases of Classification
sections.description: Specific rules are followed to find similarities among options in the classification process.

key_concepts.explanation: An inherent property found equally in all given options except one.
The specific option that does not share the common characteristic of the rest of the group.

sections.title: Steps to Solve
sections.description: A systematic strategy to solve classification questions in exams with accuracy and speed.

steps.title: Analyze Options
steps.detail: Carefully read all given options and look for potential logical relationships among them.

steps.title: Identify the Group
steps.detail: Find a rule or pattern that binds all options except one into a logical group.

steps.title: Isolate the Odd One
steps.detail: Select the option that does not follow the rule or pattern of the identified group.

sections.title: Word Classification
sections.description: A group of words is given, which are related to each other based on meaning, usage, or general knowledge.

results: All options might be synonyms of each other while one gives a different meaning.
Options might be pairs of antonyms, out of which one pair could be incorrect.
The odd one could be based on countries and capitals, currencies, or scientific names.
Classification based on young ones of animals, their sounds, or habitats.
Variation can be found based on tools and their users, or workplaces.

sections.title: Number Classification
sections.description: Involves finding the odd one out based on mathematical properties and operations of numbers.

results: All numbers except one might be even or odd.
All numbers in the group except one could be prime numbers or composite numbers.
Options can be in the form of perfect squares (like n^2) or perfect cubes (like n^3).
The pattern can also be in the form of n^2 + 1, n^2 - 1, or n^3 + n.
All numbers might be completely divisible by a specific number, except one.
The sum of digits might be divisible by a specific number.

sections.title: Letter Classification
sections.description: Classification is done based on the positional value or characteristics of letters in the English alphabet.

results: A group of letters might have an equal forward or backward jump between their place values (e.g., +2, +3, or -1).
Options might use only vowels (A, E, I, O, U) or only consonants.
The number of vowels in a particular word might differ from the other words.
Pairs of letters might be opposite to each other in the alphabet series (e.g., A-Z, B-Y, C-X).
